name: Myanmar
genZNote: Myanmar changed its own name from 'Burma' in 1989, and depending who you ask internationally, either name is still in use — a small naming dispute that quietly tells you a lot about the country's contested politics.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The largest country in mainland Southeast Asia, bordering India and Bangladesh to the west, China to the north and east, and Laos and Thailand to the east.
Geography ranges from the Himalayan foothills in the north to the fertile Irrawaddy River delta and a long Bay of Bengal / Andaman Sea coastline in the south.
Historically also known as Burma; the ruling authorities renamed the country Myanmar in 1989, a change not universally adopted internationally.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Burmese is the official language; the country is highly ethnically diverse, with the Bamar majority alongside Shan, Karen, Rakhine, Rohingya, and many other groups.
Theravada Buddhism is the majority religion and central to cultural life, visible in thousands of pagodas across the country, including the Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon.
Home to one of the world's longest-running internal armed conflicts, with numerous ethnic armed organisations active in border regions for decades.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: The military (the Tatmadaw) seized power in a coup on 1 February 2021, ousting the elected civilian government led by Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD), which had won the 2020 election.

The junta held multi-phase parliamentary elections in December 2025-January 2026, under a state of emergency, with major opposition parties (including the NLD) banned; independent observers, the UN, and several democracies widely characterised the vote as neither free nor fair.
In April 2026, parliament elected junta leader Senior General Min Aung Hlaing as president, installing a nominally civilian administration while the military retains effective control.

Civil conflict between the military and a range of ethnic armed organisations and pro-democracy resistance forces has continued since the 2021 coup, with the junta controlling only part of the country's territory.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Ongoing conflict and political instability have significantly strained healthcare infrastructure and access, particularly in contested border regions.
The country's biodiversity — including the Irrawaddy dolphin and extensive teak forests — has made it a focus of regional conservation and forestry science.
Displacement and instability have driven a significant loss of skilled professionals, including in medicine and science, in the years since the coup.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations and ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations), though ASEAN has restricted the junta's participation in some official summits since the coup.
China has provided significant diplomatic and economic backing to the military government, viewing stability in Myanmar as important to its regional infrastructure and border interests.
Western democracies and the EU have generally maintained sanctions and limited engagement with the junta, citing human rights concerns and the 2021 coup.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India shares a long land border and cultural/historical ties with Myanmar, and pursues pragmatic engagement with the ruling authorities, partly driven by concerns over cross-border insurgency, refugee flows, and connectivity projects.
India has invested in connectivity infrastructure such as the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, intended to link India's northeast with Myanmar's Sittwe port.
Myanmar is a key partner in India's 'Act East' policy, linking South Asia with Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: The economy has suffered severe disruption since the 2021 coup, with sanctions, conflict, and capital flight sharply affecting growth and investment.
Key sectors include agriculture (notably rice), natural gas exports, timber, and gemstones (Myanmar is a major global source of jade and rubies).
China remains a dominant trade and investment partner, including for energy pipelines and border trade.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Thousands of Buddhist pagodas, most famously the Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon and the temple plains of Bagan.
A prolonged pro-democracy struggle, symbolised internationally by Aung San Suu Kyi and the National League for Democracy.
Major global source of jade and rubies, and significant natural gas reserves.
One of the world's longest-running internal armed conflicts, involving numerous ethnic armed organisations.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Myanmar Kyat (MMK).
An agriculture-based economy (notably rice) with significant natural-resource wealth including jade, gems, and natural gas.
Development has been constrained by decades of political instability and international sanctions.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to extensive teak forests and the Irrawaddy River, central to the country's ecology and agriculture.
Significant biodiversity in its northern mountainous regions bordering the Himalayas.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Ruled by successive Burmese kingdoms before becoming a British colony in the 19th century.
Gained independence in 1948; has experienced repeated periods of military rule since a 1962 coup.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1948 independence from Britain.
A gradual, partial transition toward civilian democratic governance began around 2011 but was reversed by a military coup in February 2021.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Traditional Burmese martial art Lethwei and Buddhist pagoda architecture (notably Bagan's thousands of ancient temples) are culturally significant.
Bagan is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with one of the world's densest concentrations of Buddhist temples.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of ASEAN and the UN.
Its military government has faced significant international scrutiny and sanctions following the 2021 coup.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Myanmar (formerly Burma) is the largest mainland Southeast Asian country, currently under military-dominated rule following a 2021 coup and a widely disputed 2025-26 election.
keyFacts: Capital: Naypyidaw. Currency: Myanmar Kyat. Official language: Burmese.
Military coup: 1 February 2021, ousting Aung San Suu Kyi's elected NLD government.
Junta-run elections held December 2025-January 2026; widely criticised as neither free nor fair.
Min Aung Hlaing became president via parliament in April 2026, under continued military control.
commonConfusion: Myanmar's CAPITAL is Naypyidaw, not Yangon — Yangon is the largest city and former capital, but the capital was relocated to Naypyidaw in 2005.

highYieldFacts: Military coup: 1 February 2021; capital Naypyidaw (not Yangon, the former capital and largest city).
Min Aung Hlaing became president in April 2026 following a junta-run, widely disputed election.
India's Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project connects India's northeast to Myanmar's Sittwe port, part of India's 'Act East' policy.
commonTraps: Assuming Myanmar's 2025-26 elections restored full civilian democratic rule — international observers and the UN widely disputed the vote's legitimacy, and the military retains effective control.
mustRemember: Myanmar: largest mainland SE Asian country, military-controlled since the 2021 coup, major jade/ruby/natural gas exporter, key India 'Act East' partner.
